sections.html: A small knifefish (maximum length up to 20 cm) from Venezuela. It is a very nice and peaceful species. Suggested common name: Marbled Knifefish.
This species is only rarely imported, and only a few specimens could be obtained. Available size: 8–10 cm.

Regarding water chemistry the fish seem to be undemanding. However, soft and acid water should be preferred over hard and alkaline water. The water temperature should be a little higher than usual, about 26–28°C.
Knifefishes are most active at dawn, so the tank should not be too brightly lit and should contain a good number of hiding places.
The fish feed basically on Tubifex and frozen fish food.
Like all South American knifefishes, this species is weakly electric and communicates with conspecifics via electrical impulses. These impulses are also used for orientation.

The genus Adontosternarchus currently comprises four accepted species, which can best be distinguished by differences in head profile combined with the shape of the mouth.

Adontosternarchus: ancient Greek, means "Sternarchus without teeth"; Sternarchus is another genus of knifefish. clarkae: dedication name for Ms. Kate Clark, who was the first collector of the species.
